extracted.intended_audience: European news organisations, journalists, newsroom leaders, media funders, and programme applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and programme design elements for supporting and practising engaged journalism in Europe — i.e., journalism that centres community engagement to empower communities and improve public life. Describes programme components (funding, coaching, events, resources) and concrete engagement practices from grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of engaged journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaged journalism — reporting that empowers communities and their conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the programme's central concept and proposed solution to pressures on revenue, attention, trust and independence in European journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement centrality
rubrics_metrics.description: News organisations that place community engagement at the heart of their strategy are making significant progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being community-centred is treated as a key evaluative dimension: organisations should design strategy and operations with community engagement as a core priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on people’s lives through information
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists have a key role to play in improving people’s lives through access to information, data, and perspectives that build bridges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should aim to empower communities practically (access to information) and socially (building bridges between groups). Impact on audiences’ lives is an implied quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for revenue and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding: €600k of grants supported new revenue and sustainability for European organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustainability and the development of new revenue streams are explicit programme goals; grant support is a mechanism to evaluate and promote these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching and capacity building
rubrics_metrics.description: Coaching for grantees and the wider journalism community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing coaching is part of the programme’s approach to improving practice and capacity; effectiveness can be assessed by uptake, quality of coaching, and subsequent organisational change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer mentorship network
rubrics_metrics.description: A peer mentorship network, connecting legacy newsrooms with start-ups and emerging media organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-to-peer learning and mentorship across different types of organisations is highlighted as a criterion for strengthening engaged journalism; success measured by connections made and knowledge transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and events as learning tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources & events: meet-ups across Europe, playbooks and case studies of successes and failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes should produce and share practical resources (playbooks, case studies) and host events to disseminate lessons; importantly, include failures as learning material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining an engaged journalism database
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaged Journalism in Europe database — 189 European news organisations, from Belgium to Ukraine, that will inspire your community engagement work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curating a database of examples is promoted as a tool to inspire and benchmark community engagement practice across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live events to deepen audience understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Through its live podcast events Hungarian platform, G7.hu, is developing a better understanding of its readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using live/on-the-ground events (e.g., podcasts) to engage audiences and gather insights about reader needs and perspectives is presented as an effective practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioning strategy to amplify underrepresented voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Chai Khana uses its commissioning strategy: investing in journalists and filmmakers giving a voice to underrepresented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate commissioning to include underrepresented voices is a criterion for engaged journalism; assess by diversity of contributors and the extent to which stories amplify marginalized perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform use for advocacy and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Dose.mk is making decision makers aware of the challenges affecting vulnerable citizens by using its platform to advocate for change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using journalism platforms to surface issues and influence decision-makers is presented as an outcome of engaged journalism; impact on policy/awareness is an evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth media training to build social cohesion
rubrics_metrics.description: Radio Feral is using youth media training workshops to help young people from different ethnic groups find common ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and participatory media activities aimed at youth and inter-group dialogue are promoted as engagement practices that foster social cohesion; evaluate by participation and cross-group outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training next-generation freelancers (skills & safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: OC Media is training the next generation of freelance journalists: the training covers basic journalism skills, safety and how to report on different topics in the region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity-building for freelancers—including core skills and safety training—is a criterion for sustaining engaged reporting, especially in fragile contexts; measure by skill uptake and safety preparedness.
